core_question: You pay with a $50 bill for a purchase totaling $37.65. How much change do you receive?
persona: tired and blunt; writing terse one-liners

messages.content: So I paid with a 50 dollar bill and the purchase was 37.65. I need to figure out my change.
When you pay with more money than something costs, what happens to the difference?
You get change back. So I gotta subtract?
Does subtracting the cost from what you handed over make sense for figuring out what comes back to you?
Yeah. I don't have time to explain this. What's the change?
You've got the right operation in mind—so can you do the subtraction yourself?
This is ridiculous. Just one word. The amount.
Haven't you already done all the thinking needed—what's stopping you from doing the arithmetic?
Okay, fine. I worked it out and I know what my change is now.
Exactly—and didn't it feel faster when you just worked it out yourself instead of waiting for an answer?
Will you remember this the next time you're calculating change?
